question.question:
Apply only this fictional scenario-local capital policy. A bank has gross common equity of 90 USD million, intangible assets of 28 USD million and deferred tax assets of 29 USD million. Intangibles are deducted in full. Deferred tax assets are deducted only to the extent they exceed 11 percent of gross common equity net of intangibles; this deduction is never negative. Net common equity is gross common equity minus both deductions. Current risk-weighted assets are 1250 USD million and the leverage exposure measure is 3800 USD million. Net common equity must be at least 9.5 percent of risk-weighted assets and at least 4 percent of the exposure measure, both inclusive. The bank may inject new common equity X of at least zero: X adds to gross common equity (so the deferred tax threshold is recomputed on the enlarged equity), adds 20 percent of X to risk-weighted assets, and adds X in full to the exposure measure. Find the smallest X in USD million that satisfies both constraints simultaneously. Along the way report net common equity before injection, the deferred tax deduction before injection, and the binding constraint: rwa, leverage, or none when no injection is needed (if both constraints require the same positive X, report rwa).

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 4 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd_million` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Net common equity before any injection after both deductions.
Deferred tax deduction before any injection.
Which constraint determines the minimum injection.
